summary.headline: ADF Foods Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR196.7 crore (+23.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.4%, but Middle East (GCC) exposure clouds FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to a record INR196.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR34.3 crore (17.4% margin, +190 bps) and PAT of INR25.9 crore (+57.6%). Standalone FY26 revenue grew 10.3% to INR527.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 24.8%. The Surat greenfield plant began commercial production in March 2026, but West Asia disruption stopped GCC shipments in March and April, and management cut its outlook to a conditional range if the disruption persists. Net cash surplus stands at INR78.2 crore and the final dividend is 30% of face value (60% for FY26).

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Management guided Ashoka to grow about 30-35% in FY27; FY26 Ashoka revenue was about INR308 crore per an analyst's calculation that management did not dispute. Core markets are North America (incl. Canada), UK and Europe, with Australia and New Zealand also growing.

segments.name: Truly Indian (mainstream US brand)
segments.commentary: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well. Listed in about 3,000 US stores including Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons and Whole Foods; repeat rotations are seen at some Costco divisions.

segments.name: B2B and private label
segments.commentary: B2B and private label make up about 20% of revenue. Distribution business added new regional brands and Ashoka SKUs (staples, oils, flour), with SKUs rising from about 440 to about 600.

segments.name: GCC / Middle East
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue (described as under 15%). Shipments were nil in March and about 80-85% of GCC business was lost, with only 1-2 ports operating in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore, conditional on West Asia stabilising within about a month; management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues.
If GCC contribution stays at zero, FY27 growth is about 12-15% (roughly INR800-850 crore); with GCC normalised, growth of 30%+ and the INR925-1,000 crore band.
Surat plant expected to contribute INR40-50 crore revenue in FY27; full capacity implies upwards of INR200-250 crore (Phase 2 included), with full utilisation targeted in year 3.
Management expects to maintain high-teen consolidated EBITDA margins; Surat margins at full capacity expected to be similar to existing facilities.
Freight costs up about 3-4% of revenue in March; management said this is expected to ease over about the next two months. Analyst was told to add about 1 percentage point of freight in the base.
PLI incentive expected to be similar in FY27 (about INR16 crore) and is the final year of the scheme.
Capex of INR20-25 crore in FY27 (pizza base line, Surat balance payments), plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking; a further US warehouse is planned around Q3 FY27.
Potential INR30 crore quarterly revenue risk from GCC on a run-rate basis, as an analyst framed it and management confirmed.
capex_capacity: Approximately INR124 crore capex over the last 2 years across Nadiad, Nashik brownfield and Surat greenfield; Surat total investment including Phase 2 is a little above INR100 crore.
Surat Phase 1 (2 product lines) commenced production in the third week of March 2026; Phase 2 adds a product line (pizza base) in Q3 FY27.
Surat utilisation expected at about 35-40% in Phase 1 during FY27; Phase 2 contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27.
Average capacity utilisation across product lines was about 70-75% in FY26.
US warehouse: freezer space above 100% utilised (using outside storage); ambient space about 85% utilised. Another distribution centre planned, probably in Q3 FY27.
Debottlenecking at Nadiad and Nashik (flatbread and snack lines) drove most of the FY26 volume growth.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, with the balance from product mix and rupee depreciation; management said prices were not increased.
Truly Indian initial traction is mainly distribution-led, with some repeats at Costco and other chains; management sees the Indian ethnic category at an inflection point in the US mainstream channel.
No impact seen from GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic) on demand; the whole range is vegetarian and vegan.
GCC shipments were nil in March 2026 because shipping lines were not taking containers. Other markets saw longer transit times and higher freight rates but no loss of sales.
Freight costs rose sharply in March 2026 as vessels were jammed and US routes lengthened; the company shares freight cost with GCC distributors 50:50 on those routes.
Tariff refund: applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million following a Supreme Court directive; nothing received in FY26, and any refund will be accrued in the year received.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 guidance of INR925-1,000 crore reconcile with the growth drivers, given Ashoka and Truly Indian?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR925-1,000 crore band, conditional on the Middle East reopening. Ashoka is expected to grow 30-35% and Truly Indian INR75-80 crore. With zero GCC, growth is 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East (GCC) impact and worst-case scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC is under 15% of revenue. About 80-85% of GCC business has been lost, with nil March shipments. In the zero-GCC case, FY27 growth is about 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Surat plant ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Surat contribution is INR40-50 crore; full capacity implies INR200-250 crore once Phase 2 is complete. Full utilisation is targeted in year 3.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight-cost increase should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rose by about 3-4% of revenue in March. The CFO said about 1 percentage point should be added to the base, with normalisation expected over about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and total Surat spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat total is a little above INR100 crore. FY27 capex is INR20-25 crore (pizza line and balance payments) plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Will PLI incentive continue after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme, expected at a similar level (about INR16 crore). The scheme covered 50% of marketing spend.

risks_watch: West Asia / GCC disruption: about 15% of revenue, with nil March shipments and only 1-2 ports open in April; guidance depends on normalisation within about 1-2 months.
Freight and logistics costs: March spike of about 3-4% of revenue; management expects normalisation but this is unproven.
Loss of PLI incentive after FY27 (about INR16 crore per year) will remove a support to margins.
Surat ramp-up: Phase 2 starts in Q3 FY27 and contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27; execution risk.
Freezer capacity in the US warehouse is above 100%, which requires outside storage and a new distribution centre.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 and FY26 results and on brand momentum, but cautious and conditional on guidance. Management repeatedly tied FY27 targets to a West Asia recovery and said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues; some answers on Middle East figures and the revenue bridge were vague.
key_quotes: So the Middle East has been -- I mean, because of the current situation in the month of March and April, we've not been able to service that market apart from a few ports because there are no shipping companies which are taking containers there.
So if the situation in the Middle East continues, of course, it will have an impact, and then we will look at revising our guidance.
The majority of the growth has come through with volume growth.
Surat total investment in Surat with Phase 2 completion will be a little above INR100 crores.
